language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hello, my name is Akiel. I live in Jamaica and I enjoy surfing with my friends. My father is a mycologist who specializes in the study of fungi.
When I'm not surfing, I like to help my father collect and categorize fungi. Fungi can be found all over the world—in wet tropical forests, hot deserts and even on Antartica.

So no matter where you live, you can find fungi. Did you know that there are over a 100,000 types of fungi? That's a lot of fungi to discover! Would you like to help us identify and organize our collections?

So no matter where you live, you can find fungi. Did you know that there are over a 100,000 types of fungi? That's a lot of fungi to discover! Would you like to help us identify and organize our collections?
We used to believe fungi were plants and belonged to the Plant kingdom. But now we know that fungi belong to their own kingdom.

My father is going to present his collection at our local school. He has many photographs of fungi but they got mixed up with photos of plants! Can you help us sort the pictures into the correct kingdoms?

Fungi are so called "heterotrophs". That is a big word but it simply means that fungi get their food by absorbing nutrients from other things.

For example: when there is mold on your bread, this fungi is absorbing the nutrients from the bread. It's eating! Some fungi absorb their food from dead matter such as rotting fruit, dying trees, or dead animals.

This can be very helpful for recycling dead matter. Other fungi get nutrients from living things. These types of fungi can be harmful to us. Can you help me create a journal of helpful fungi and harmful fungi?
